engagements.title: Delegation morning huddle
engagements.venue: Meridia Delegation Office, Blue Zone Level 2
objectives: Confirm today's negotiating priorities and any overnight text changes
Align lines for the Germany and Brazil bilaterals
talkingPoints: Overnight: draft cover decision now references 'phase-down of unabated fossil fuels' — hold our position for stronger language
Finance is the day's battleground — keep the $300bn/yr floor as our anchor number
Press likely to ask about our new 2035 NDC — stick to agreed line, no new numbers
redLines: Do not pre-announce the adaptation pledge before the Thursday plenary
engagements.desiredOutcome: Team aligned; Minister clear on the three asks for the day.

engagements.title: Bilateral: Germany
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 4B, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Dr. Klara Böhm
counterpart.title: Federal Minister for Economic Affairs & Climate Action
counterpart.profile: Career economist, second COP as minister. Pragmatic, detail-driven, pushes hard on carbon-market integrity. Values punctuality and concrete follow-ups. Good personal rapport with the Minister since the Berlin visit.

objectives: Secure Germany's co-sponsorship of the adaptation finance text
Explore a bilateral green-hydrogen partnership
talkingPoints: Thank Germany for €50m contribution to the Loss & Damage Fund — momentum we want to build on
Ask: will Germany co-sponsor our adaptation finance amendment? We need a G7 anchor
Offer: Meridia can host a green-hydrogen pilot; propose officials meet in Q4
Article 6 — we're aligned on strong integrity rules; coordinate floor positions
redLines: Avoid committing to a specific hydrogen investment figure
Do not link adaptation support to any trade concessions
engagements.desiredOutcome: Germany verbally agrees to co-sponsor the adaptation text; officials tasked on hydrogen.

engagements.title: High Ambition Coalition ministerial
objectives: Keep the coalition united behind a 1.5°C-aligned cover decision
Position Meridia as a bridge between developed and vulnerable members
talkingPoints: Reaffirm: no backsliding on the 1.5°C temperature goal in the cover text
Push for a collective call to peak global emissions before 2027
Signal Meridia will help broker language with the G77 on finance
redLines: Do not isolate the small-island members on the mitigation timeline
engagements.desiredOutcome: Coalition agrees a joint line on 1.5°C to carry into plenary.

engagements.title: Bilateral: Brazil (COP31 Presidency)

counterpart.name: Sr. Rafael Mendonça
counterpart.title: Minister of the Environment & Climate Change
counterpart.profile: As COP President, focused on landing a balanced package. Warm, relationship-first style. Sensitive about Amazon/forest framing. Wants visible wins on forests and finance to define the presidency.

objectives: Understand the Presidency's landing zone on finance
Offer Meridia's support to broker the adaptation package
talkingPoints: Congratulate the Presidency on the forests initiative — Meridia wants to be an early partner
Ask: what's the Presidency's realistic landing zone on the finance number?
Offer: we can help bring vulnerable states along if the text protects adaptation
Flag: our red line is retaining the 1.5°C language — we'll defend it publicly
redLines: Do not criticise the Presidency's process in front of others
Avoid any comment on internal Brazilian politics
engagements.desiredOutcome: Clear read on the Presidency's finance landing zone; Meridia positioned as a trusted broker.

engagements.title: Media doorstep
objectives: Project ambition and unity; avoid new commitments
talkingPoints: Meridia is here to keep 1.5°C alive and secure real money for adaptation
We're encouraged by the Presidency's leadership on forests
If pressed on our NDC: 'We'll announce our updated plan at the right moment this week'
redLines: No new numbers on finance or NDC
Do not comment on any other country's domestic policy
engagements.desiredOutcome: Clean, on-message clips; no unintended headlines.

engagements.title: Climate Finance roundtable
objectives: Build a critical mass behind the $300bn/yr adaptation floor
Test appetite for a new grants-based instrument
talkingPoints: Anchor: adaptation finance must have a $300bn/yr floor by 2030, grants-based not loans
Vulnerable states cannot take on more debt for a crisis they did not cause
Propose: a dedicated grants window under the existing fund — no new bureaucracy
Ask developed partners to signal replenishment numbers this week
redLines: Do not accept loan-based instruments as counting toward the floor
engagements.desiredOutcome: At least three donor countries signal support for a grants window.

engagements.title: Bilateral: Tuvalu (Pacific SIDS)
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 2A, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Hon. Tavita Faleolo
counterpart.title: Minister for Climate Resilience
counterpart.profile: Passionate advocate for island survival; speaks powerfully on existential risk. Expects solidarity, not sympathy. Deep expertise on loss & damage. A key voice Meridia wants firmly alongside us.

objectives: Reaffirm Meridia's solidarity with Pacific SIDS
Coordinate a joint push on loss & damage disbursement
talkingPoints: Meridia stands with the Pacific — your survival is non-negotiable in this text
Propose a joint statement: the Loss & Damage Fund must start disbursing in 2026, not 2027
We'll amplify SIDS priorities in the High Ambition Coalition
Ask: what one outcome would make COP31 a success for Tuvalu?
redLines: Do not appear to trade away SIDS priorities for the finance deal
engagements.desiredOutcome: Agreement to issue a joint loss & damage statement Wednesday.

engagements.title: Article 6 carbon markets — technical huddle
engagements.venue: Meridia Delegation Office, Blue Zone Level 2
objectives: Decide Meridia's fallback position on Article 6.4 integrity rules
talkingPoints: Where can we compromise on baselines without weakening environmental integrity?
Confirm our line on avoiding double-counting — this stays firm
Brief the Minister on tomorrow's EU bilateral asks
redLines: No agreement that permits double-counting of credits
engagements.desiredOutcome: Agreed fallback position documented for negotiators.

engagements.title: Bilateral: European Union
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 4B, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Commissioner Elena Novak
counterpart.title: European Commissioner for Climate Action
counterpart.profile: Speaks for 27 member states; highly strategic. Focused on carbon border measures and finance credibility. Prefers structured agendas. Can unlock significant finance if the ambition case is made well.

objectives: Seek EU flexibility on the grants-based adaptation window
Manage concerns about carbon border measures on Meridia exports
talkingPoints: Welcome EU leadership on ambition; we want the EU as our finance partner
Ask: can the EU support a grants-based adaptation window, not just loans?
Raise sensitively: carbon border measures are hitting our exporters — seek a dialogue
Offer: Meridia will back strong Article 6 integrity rules the EU cares about
redLines: Do not accept linkage between finance and our trade position
Avoid public criticism of the EU carbon border mechanism
engagements.desiredOutcome: EU opens door to grants window; agrees officials-level trade dialogue.

engagements.title: Loss & Damage Fund — Board session
objectives: Push for disbursement to begin in 2026
Protect grants-based, direct-access design
talkingPoints: The Fund exists — now it must deliver; first disbursements should flow in 2026
Direct access for vulnerable states is essential; minimise intermediaries
Support simplified access for small island and least-developed states
Meridia will contribute technical experts to the operating committee
redLines: Do not support a design that routes everything through existing slow channels
engagements.desiredOutcome: Board agrees a 2026 disbursement timeline and simplified access track.

engagements.title: National Statement — High-Level Segment
objectives: Deliver Meridia's headline positions to the full conference
Announce the updated 2035 NDC
talkingPoints: Announce: Meridia's updated NDC — 60% emissions cut by 2035 (agreed line, deliver exactly)
Call for a $300bn/yr adaptation finance floor, grants-based
Defend 1.5°C as the line the world cannot cross
Solidarity with SIDS and LDCs — loss & damage must deliver now
redLines: Deliver the NDC figure exactly as cleared — no deviation
Keep to the 3-minute time limit
engagements.desiredOutcome: Statement delivered cleanly; NDC lands as a credible ambition signal.

engagements.title: Bilateral: Indonesia
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 1C, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Ibu Sari Wibowo
counterpart.title: Minister of Environment & Forestry
counterpart.profile: Leads on forests, peatlands and just transition from coal. Balances development and climate pressures. Interested in South-South cooperation and blended finance. Warm but firm on sovereignty over resources.

objectives: Explore South-South cooperation on forests and just transition
Coordinate G77 positioning on finance
talkingPoints: Propose a South-South knowledge partnership on peatland and forest restoration
Align G77 messaging: finance must be additional, predictable and grants-based
Explore joint interest in a just-transition financing facility for coal regions
Reaffirm respect for sovereign resource decisions while raising ambition
redLines: Avoid any suggestion of conditions on Indonesia's domestic resource policy
engagements.desiredOutcome: Agreement to launch an officials-level forests partnership.

engagements.title: Just Transition side event (panel)
objectives: Showcase Meridia's just-transition model
Attract partners to our transition financing facility
talkingPoints: Share Meridia's story: retraining coal workers into renewables manufacturing
A just transition is a political precondition for ambition — no one left behind
Invite partners to co-fund our just-transition facility
Keep it human — lead with the workers' stories, not just numbers
redLines: Do not overstate results — stick to verified figures in the brief
engagements.desiredOutcome: Strong panel; at least one partner expresses interest in co-funding.

engagements.title: Bilateral: United Kingdom
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 3A, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Rt Hon. James Whitfield MP
counterpart.title: Secretary of State for Energy Security & Net Zero
counterpart.profile: Politically focused on clean-power investment and finance mobilisation. Quick, outcome-oriented, likes a concrete deliverable to announce. Strong on mobilising private finance and multilateral bank reform.

objectives: Enlist UK support for multilateral development bank reform
Coordinate on mobilising private adaptation finance
talkingPoints: Thank the UK for its clean-power leadership; we want to partner on finance
Ask: will the UK champion MDB reform to unlock climate lending at scale?
Explore a joint initiative to de-risk private adaptation investment
Coordinate High Ambition Coalition lines for the final days
redLines: Do not commit Meridia to any private-finance guarantee mechanism yet
engagements.desiredOutcome: UK agrees to co-champion MDB reform language in the cover text.

engagements.title: Bilateral: India
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 4B, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Shri Arjun Nair
counterpart.title: Minister of Environment, Forest & Climate Change
counterpart.profile: Champions equity and 'common but differentiated responsibilities'. Strong on solar and development-first framing. Influential across the G77. Values respect for historical responsibility and development space.

objectives: Align on equity framing without splitting from the High Ambition Coalition
Explore solar and grids cooperation
talkingPoints: Acknowledge equity and differentiated responsibility — we share this framing
Seek India's help to bridge G77 and High Ambition Coalition on the cover text
Propose cooperation on solar manufacturing and regional grids
Emphasise: developed countries must deliver finance first
redLines: Do not let equity framing be used to weaken the 1.5°C language
engagements.desiredOutcome: India agrees to help broker G77 buy-in on the cover decision.

engagements.title: AOSIS coalition meeting
objectives: Lock in a unified small-island position for the endgame
Confirm the joint loss & damage statement
talkingPoints: Reaffirm Meridia's solidarity — we will not let 1.5°C be traded away
Confirm the joint loss & damage disbursement statement for release today
Coordinate red lines for the final cover-decision negotiations
Agree who speaks for the group in the closing plenary
redLines: Do not undercut AOSIS unity in side conversations with larger powers
engagements.desiredOutcome: Unified AOSIS endgame position and speaking plan agreed.

engagements.title: Bilateral: China
engagements.venue: Bilateral Room 5A, Blue Zone Pavilion Hall

counterpart.name: Mr. Li Wenqiang
counterpart.title: Special Envoy for Climate Change
counterpart.profile: Highly experienced negotiator; measured and strategic. Focused on renewables scale-up and differentiated responsibility. Prefers quiet diplomacy over public asks. Decisive on whether the endgame lands.

objectives: Understand China's bottom line on the cover decision
Explore cooperation on affordable renewables supply chains
talkingPoints: Recognise China's scale in renewables — vital to global success
Ask, quietly: what does China need to accept stronger cover-decision language?
Explore access to affordable solar and battery supply for Meridia's transition
Emphasise our shared interest in a stable, predictable finance architecture
redLines: Keep asks private — no public pressure that could harden positions
Do not stray into non-climate bilateral issues
engagements.desiredOutcome: Clear read on China's endgame bottom line; renewables dialogue opened.
engagements.staffContact: Bilaterals Desk — S. Rahman / Lead Negotiator

engagements.title: Cover decision — closing negotiations
objectives: Hold the 1.5°C and adaptation-finance lines in the final text
Land an outcome Meridia can publicly support
talkingPoints: Non-negotiable: retain explicit 1.5°C language
Push to the end for the grants-based adaptation finance floor
Support the Presidency's package if our two red lines hold
Coordinate live with AOSIS and the High Ambition Coalition on the floor
redLines: Do not agree to a text that drops 1.5°C or converts adaptation finance to loans
engagements.desiredOutcome: Final text retains 1.5°C and a grants-based adaptation commitment.

engagements.title: Closing press conference
objectives: Frame the outcome as a step forward driven by ambition and solidarity
talkingPoints: Lead with the win: 1.5°C held, and real movement on adaptation finance
Credit the coalition and SIDS partners — this was collective
Be honest where it fell short, but forward-looking on next steps
Thank the Brazilian Presidency for a balanced outcome
redLines: Do not overclaim; keep to agreed outcome lines
No criticism of specific countries by name
engagements.desiredOutcome: Positive, credible closing narrative; clips reinforce Meridia's leadership.
